inputs.share_count_basis: Shares issued less treasury shares at 30 June 2026 = 218,072,613 (H1 2026 report, notes on earnings per share). No dilutive securities, so basic = diluted. Held FLAT: there is no SBC to charge, and the EUR750m 2026-27 buyback is cash-funded from the surplus liquidity already counted in the bridge, so retiring shares would double-count that cash.

inputs.wacc_rationale: EUR flows discounted at a EUR rate: 10y Bund ~2.7% + beta ~0.8 (consumer staples, low leverage) x 5.5% ERP = ~7.1%, rounded to 7.0%. Net-cash balance sheet, so WACC = cost of equity. Same WACC in all three scenarios; cyclical/turnaround risk is carried in the scenario flows and weights, not in a discount-rate premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost: lease cash (principal EUR77m + ~EUR6m interest, FY2025 cash flow statement) charged as lease_cost_pct_path ~0.85% of revenue inside EBIT; da_pct_path is D&A EXCLUDING right-of-use depreciation (FY2025 D&A 328 less ~75 ROU = ~253, 2.6% of revenue); lease liabilities (~EUR190m) EXCLUDED from net debt.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated (100%). NCI charged once, in the equity bridge, at ~EUR17m/yr attributable profit x ~18 = EUR300m (balance-sheet NCI of EUR9m understates the economic claim). FY0 calibration: FY2025 EBITDA 1,648 - lease 80 - D&A ex-ROU 253 = EBIT 1,315 x (1-30.5%) = 914 operating NOPAT + ~40 after-tax financial income - ~20 NCI = ~934 vs reported attributable net income 939.
inputs.fx_note: Single currency: EUR statements, EUR XETRA quote. No FX bridge.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF, routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md row 'Operating company, non-US or cyclical: consumer' with owner-fcf-adaptations applied (EUR WACC, lease treatment B, NCI in bridge, matching-asset rule for securities, SBC-zero). First valuation of this ticker (no MEMORY.md entry). Beiersdorf is a branded consumer-staples manufacturer (Consumer ~83% of sales: NIVEA, Derma/Eucerin/Aquaphor, Health Care, La Prairie; tesa adhesives ~17%) -- a normal FCF business, not a financial or holdco. NET CASH: cash 1,282 + current securities 1,435 + non-current securities 1,566 = 4,283 at 30-Jun-2026 (H1 2026 balance sheet); company-defined net liquidity (after loans and all lease liabilities) is 4,045, implying current loan liabilities of ~48 after ~190 of leases. net_debt = 48 - 4,283 = -4,235. Interest income (FY2025 EUR57m) stripped from the FCF base and the securities that earn it are in the bridge (matching-asset rule). last_fcf = reported FCF 322 (OCF 785 - capex 463) - SBC 0 - interest income 57 = 265; FY2025 FCF was depressed by a receivables build (FY2024 was 794), so the forward build is from components, not this base. Buybacks: EUR501m in each of FY2024 and FY2025, EUR32m in H1 2026 under the new EUR750m 2026-27 programme -- a funded repurchaser, but buybacks are value-neutral here (flat count, cash in bridge). TROUGH FRAMING: FY2026 is a guided trough year (Consumer organic low-single-digit decline, Consumer adj. EBIT margin >=11.0% vs 13.6% FY2025, tesa flat organic with margin slightly down; ~EUR100m incremental NIVEA marketing; management: NIVEA growth back in 2027, profitable growth from 2028). The base margin path climbs from the trough back to ~16.6% reported EBITDA, the FY2014-FY2025 decade average (range 15.4%-17.4%), not the FY2018 peak or the FY2026 trough. Reported (post-special-factors) EBITDA is used rather than 'excluding special factors', because Beiersdorf books restructuring special factors nearly every year.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: FY2014-FY2025 nominal revenue CAGR (~4.2%) and pre-COVID organic growth of 3-5%; equity CAGRs are depressed by EUR1bn of buybacks and higher dividends since FY2024, and the 5yr revenue/EPS CAGRs start from the COVID trough (FY2020)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 6.6% vs EPS 5yr CAGR 11.5% diverge by >30% relative: EPS benefits from the FY2020 COVID base and from buybacks, equity is suppressed by EUR1.0bn of FY2024-25 repurchases. Neither is a clean forward rate.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF less interest income; SBC is zero). The owner-FCF series is very lumpy (FY2020 671 -> FY2022 213 -> FY2024 722 -> FY2025 265) because of the FY2021-23 capex programme (Leipzig DC, Poland/Mexico/Brazil plants, Hamburg campus) and receivables swings, so the 5yr FCF CAGR of -17% says more about base-year choice than about the business. Reported and owner-FCF CAGRs differ only by interest income since SBC is zero.

base.narrative: Guided FY2026 trough (nominal sales ~-4% incl. ~1pp FX; reported EBITDA ~14.9%), NIVEA stabilises 2027 and grows 2028+, Derma keeps compounding, La Prairie flat-to-up; margin returns to the decade-average 16.6% by 2030.

bull.narrative: Turnaround lands early, Derma double-digit growth plus La Prairie recovery lift mix; margin settles at the FY2018 peak level of ~17.5%.

bear.narrative: NIVEA decline persists into 2027, La Prairie relapses with China/travel retail, tesa auto/electronics stay weak; marketing reinvestment becomes permanent and margin settles ~1.3pp below the decade average.

scenario_narratives.base: Management's own timetable holds. FY2026 is the trough: Consumer organic sales fall low single digits with NIVEA (~43% of group) down ~6-7% and La Prairie negative for the year, tesa flat, and the extra ~EUR100m NIVEA marketing plus negative operating leverage take reported EBITDA to ~14.9%. NIVEA stabilises in 2027 (group nominal +2%) and returns to profitable growth in 2028; Derma (Eucerin/Aquaphor, +11.7% organic in FY2025) keeps compounding on Thiamidol/Epicelline roll-outs in China, the US, India and Japan, and La Prairie's Q2 2026 return to growth holds at low single digits. Group growth recovers to the pre-COVID 4-4.5% band, then fades to 2.5%. Margin recovers to 16.6%, the FY2014-FY2025 decade average -- a mid-cycle level, neither the FY2018 peak nor the FY2026 trough. Capex steps down from the FY2022-26 build-out (Leipzig DC, Poland/Mexico/Brazil capacity, Hamburg campus) toward ~3.7% of sales.
scenario_narratives.bull: The NIVEA rebalancing (broader categories beyond face care, affordability, local autonomy) works faster than guided and NIVEA is growing again during 2027. Derma sustains double-digit growth for several more years and becomes a larger, higher-margin share of the mix; La Prairie's new leadership turns the post-2023 decline into a genuine luxury recovery as Chinese sentiment and travel retail improve; tesa benefits from an automotive and electronics upcycle. Growth runs 5-6% in 2028-2030 and margin rises to ~17.5%, the FY2018 peak, on mix and operating leverage.
scenario_narratives.bear: Guidance has now been cut twice in a year and the bear case is that it is cut again. NIVEA's decline is structural (lost share in mass skin care to local and indie brands, retailer pricing friction such as the Swiss Comco probe), so 2027 is another down year and the extra marketing becomes a permanent cost rather than an investment. La Prairie relapses with Chinese luxury and travel retail; tesa stays stuck in a weak European auto and consumer-electronics cycle with rising material costs. Growth recovers only to 2.5-3%, margin plateaus around 15.3% (about the FY2014 low), and the terminal exit is a lower 18x cap. Even here the EUR4bn net cash and staples-grade cash generation keep the business far from distress -- the bear is a de-rating of earnings power, not a solvency case.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25% because the thesis rests on an unproven 18-month NIVEA turnaround and guidance has been cut twice in about a year with Q3 due 27-Oct. Base 50% because management's 2027/2028 timetable is explicit and Derma is a demonstrated grower. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs three independent things to go right at once: NIVEA early, La Prairie/China recovery, and a tesa upcycle.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value Beiersdorf as a mid-cycle branded-staples cash generator bought at a trough, not as a smooth grower: the FY2026 guided margin is a floor-of-cycle reading, the terminal margin is the decade average, and the EUR4bn surplus liquidity (net of NCI, pensions and an operating-cash reserve) is added once while the interest it earns is stripped from the flows.
key_risks_to_valuation: NIVEA turnaround fails or slips past 2028, making the 16.6% terminal margin too high (bear path: 15.3%)
La Prairie remains hostage to Chinese luxury sentiment and travel retail
tesa automotive/electronics cycle stays weak; tesa is ~17% of sales and ~20% of adj. EBIT
Further guidance cut at the Q3 2026 update (27-Oct-2026) -- the price anchor predates it
Terminal value is the bulk of enterprise value at a 7% EUR WACC; each 1pp of WACC moves value materially (see sensitivity grid)
Majority holder maxingvest (~53%) controls capital allocation, so the surplus cash may stay on the balance sheet rather than be returned
